| `B963` | TAU DOES DOUBLE DUTY -- the one cause behind four apparently independent failures -- PLUS a scope correction caught before banking, prompted by the owner's 'are we rushing?'. THE MECHANISM: computed here, E6's diagram has exactly ONE nontrivial automorphism tau = (5,1,4,3,2,0) of order 2 swapping node pairs (0,5) and (2,4), and all 63 inner sign-gradings fix the FULL Cartan; chained with standard facts (w0 = -tau for E6, so tau != id <=> -1 not in W(E6) <=> E6 has complex representations -- which is WHY the 27 is complex; and every inner involution fixes a Cartan so the only rank-reducing involutions are OUTER, i.e. exactly tau up to inner). SO THE SAME TAU BOTH CERTIFIES THAT THE 27 IS COMPLEX AND IS THE ONLY INVOLUTION THAT CAN REDUCE RANK -- spend it on rank and you land in Fix(tau) where 27 = 27bar. Not two quantities in tension but ONE RESOURCE, and using it for either purpose spends it. IS IT AN UNCERTAINTY PRINCIPLE? NO, and the analogy is REJECTED rather than banked: an uncertainty relation needs a conjugate pair (we have one object with two roles), a quantitative bound (we have a dichotomy, no trade-off curve, no rank-5 half-chiral state), both quantities simultaneously meaningful but unsharp (ours are mutually exclusive), and a state space carrying the variances (we have none) -- and reality type is DISCRETE (Frobenius-Schur +1/-1/0) so there is no continuous amount of chirality to trade against rank. THE SCOPE CORRECTION, the reason this arc exists: I was about to bank the sharper-sounding claim that THE OBJECT HAS NO INTERMEDIATE REGIME -- that any chirality at all forces full E6 closure. B576 read carefully says only 'along any integrable deformation OF THE GEOMETRIC REPRESENTATION with a nonzero theta-odd component, the Zariski closure is forced to full E6(C)', and its mechanism is the BLOCK-SUM LEMMA, which works precisely because such deformations CONTAIN THE PRINCIPAL sl2 (centralizer zero in e6, multiplicity-one blocks). So the threshold HOLDS for deformations containing the principal sl2 and is NOT established for arbitrary representations of pi_1 into E6 -- and specifically NOT for the FINITE-IMAGE representations (A4, D5, S5) that L133 was about, since a finite image contains no principal sl2 at all. DOES THE CONCLUSION SURVIVE? YES, but by a DIFFERENT argument: the finite-image case is closed INDEPENDENTLY by B959's torality step (elementary abelian rank <= 2 => toral => rank 6), not by any threshold. So the no-go stands while the unified 'no intermediate regime' framing does NOT -- two arguments, not one, and saying otherwise would have been a FALSE UNIFICATION, the most attractive kind of error this programme makes. NOTHING IN THIS ARC OVERTURNS B798's LAW OR ITS COST ESTIMATE. (3) THE SOLVER FAILED ITS OWN GATE (recover B922's r = 4.9000853730625213014795758 or claim nothing): M=40 gives g ~ 1e26, M=80 is smooth with no sign change.
